variants.title: Double-click checkout
variants.context: A shopper double-clicks Pay and two POSTs create two orders and two charges.
variants.constraint: The client may retry; the user meant one purchase.
variants.question: What API property prevents duplicate charges?
variants.expectedPattern: An idempotency key so the second POST returns the original order instead of a new charge.
wrongChoices: Disable the button only, with no server key
Accept both POSTs as separate orders
Increase the timeout so users click more

variants.title: Webhook delivered twice
variants.context: A payment provider sends the same paid event twice after a timeout.
variants.question: How should the webhook handler behave?
variants.expectedPattern: Dedupe on event id and treat a second delivery as a no-op success.
wrongChoices: Credit the wallet twice
Return 500 so the provider retries again
Ignore event ids

variants.title: PUT vs POST for updates
variants.context: Clients retry a POST that increments a counter and the counter drifts.
variants.question: Which HTTP model is safer?
variants.expectedPattern: Make the operation idempotent (PUT/UPSERT or key-protected POST), not a bare increment.
wrongChoices: POST increment with no key
GET that mutates state
Client-only retry without server dedupe

variants.title: Key reused for a different body
variants.context: The same idempotency key is sent with a different cart total.
variants.constraint: Keys must bind to one request payload.
variants.question: What should the server return?
variants.expectedPattern: Reject the mismatch (e.g. 409) rather than silently applying a new charge under the old key.
wrongChoices: Overwrite the first charge
Ignore the body and always 200
Create a third order

variants.title: In-flight duplicate
variants.context: A retry arrives while the first charge is still processing.
variants.constraint: Two workers must not both call the card network.
variants.question: What coordination is required?
variants.expectedPattern: Lock or record the key as in-progress so the second request waits or returns the same outcome.
wrongChoices: Start a second charge in parallel
Drop the first request
No row for the key until after the network call

variants.title: Email send on retry
variants.context: A welcome email job retries after SMTP success but before ack, and the user gets two emails.
variants.constraint: SMTP is not transactional with the queue.
variants.question: How do you make the job safe?
variants.expectedPattern: Record a sent token for that user/email type before or atomically with send, and skip if already sent.
wrongChoices: Send every time the job runs
Ack before send and lose the email
Disable retries entirely as the only control

variants.title: Client-generated IDs
variants.context: Mobile creates order IDs offline and replays them after reconnect.
variants.constraint: The same ID may arrive hours later.
variants.question: What uniqueness model fits?
variants.expectedPattern: Treat client order IDs as idempotency keys with a unique constraint on persist.
wrongChoices: Server always assigns a new ID on every replay
No unique index on client order ID
Delete old orders when a replay arrives

variants.title: Partial failure after side effect
variants.context: The card is charged, then the DB write fails, then a retry charges again.
variants.constraint: The side effect happened outside your database.
variants.question: What must be stored first?
variants.expectedPattern: Persist the idempotency key and intended charge before calling the network, then complete or reconcile.
wrongChoices: Call the network first with no local key
Retry charges without checking provider references
Trust only the HTTP 200 from the first attempt

variants.title: Idempotency store expires too soon
variants.context: Keys live 60 seconds, but mobile retries after 3 minutes and a second order is created.
variants.constraint: Retry windows are longer than the TTL.
variants.question: How long should keys live?
variants.expectedPattern: Keep idempotency records at least as long as realistic client retry windows.
wrongChoices: 60-second TTL for money moves
No persistence of keys
Expire keys on first response even if the client never saw it

variants.title: DELETE is retried
variants.context: A client retries DELETE /item/9 and the second call returns 404, which the app treats as failure.
variants.question: What is the idempotent DELETE contract?
variants.expectedPattern: Treat a second DELETE as success (200/204) because the desired state is already absent.
wrongChoices: 404 as a hard error on every extra DELETE
Recreate the item so DELETE can run again
POST to delete

variants.title: GraphQL mutation without a key
variants.context: placeOrder is retried by Apollo after a timeout and two orders appear.
variants.question: What belongs on the mutation?
variants.expectedPattern: A client mutation id stored uniquely so retries return the first order.
wrongChoices: Retries with no mutation id
Idempotency only on queries
Disable the network cache and hope

variants.title: Exactly-once as a slogan
variants.context: A team claims Kafka exactly-once, then a downstream HTTP call still fires twice.
variants.constraint: External side effects are outside the broker’s EOS.
variants.question: What still has to be designed?
variants.expectedPattern: Idempotent handlers at every side-effect boundary, not only broker EOS.
wrongChoices: Assume Kafka EOS covers HTTP charges
No outbound idempotency keys
Disable acks

variants.title: Refund applied twice
variants.context: Support clicks Refund, the page times out, they click again, and the customer is paid twice.
variants.question: What should the refund API require?
variants.expectedPattern: A unique refund key per payment so a second click returns the original refund.
wrongChoices: Refund as a bare increment of a balance
No unique constraint on refund ids
Client-side disable button only

variants.title: Natural key already exists
variants.context: Creating a user by email retries and the unique index conflicts.
variants.constraint: The first request may have succeeded.
variants.question: How should the API treat the conflict?
variants.expectedPattern: Map the unique conflict to the existing user when the request is a retry of the same create.
wrongChoices: Always 500 on unique violation
Create a second user with a suffix
Delete the first user

variants.title: Non-idempotent PATCH merge
variants.context: PATCH adds +1 to quantity on each retry because it sends a delta, not the desired quantity.
variants.question: What payload is idempotent?
variants.expectedPattern: Send the desired absolute state (quantity = 3), not a relative increment.
wrongChoices: PATCH { "add": 1 } on every retry
No version field and relative updates
Apply deltas twice to be sure
